newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent cash market eases, Urals firm.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent cash market eases, Urals firm.

text.p: The Brent paper market eased lower in early trade on Tuesday, with the front May/June spread particularly weak ahead of the expiry of the May IPE contract today, traders said.

May/June traded in Singapore at a low of -30 cents, having traded at -25 cents in the U.S. aftermarket. The spread later traded back up to -25 cents in early London dealing, still five cents down on Monday's traded levels.
On the IPE, the May/June spread eased back by 10 cents to trade at -25 cents at 1000 GMT, having settled above paper market levels on Monday.
The IPE May Brent contract, which expires at the close of business on Tuesday, was trading 16 cents down at $18.03 a barrel.
The May Brent loading programme released on Tuesday morning scheduled the equivalent of 41.8 cargoes, or two full 500,000 barrel cargoes more than the revised April programme.
Traders said the higher programme was due to the longer month and a slightly lighter maintenance schedule on the Brent system than in April.
"We expected it to be a bit higher anyway so it's not too dramatic," said one.

In the Mediterranean Urals looked steady to firmer into early May as limited supplies met with good buying interest. The few sellers seen were at Dated Brent -$1.10 following Friday's trades at -$1.14 and -$1.15 a barrel.
Traders said they expected the strength to continue into early May despite more competition next month from Iraqi Kirkuk.

"Term deals should see Urals hold strong into the first part of May and then it will ease off," one said. Mediterranean refiners continued to run with low stocks. "I haven't seen any stock building except perhaps one refiner. The contango is narrowing and it isn't worth changing our policy," one said.
Syrian negotiations continued for May barrels with Syrian Light offered at dated Dated Brent -82 cents and buyers eight cents lower.
On Souedie the offer was at Dated Brent -$4.60 with the term customers looking for a rollover on the month at Dated Brent -$4.70.
Those involved in the negotiations expected levels to be agreed by the end of the week.
